failure_modes.description: Assumes surface tension gradients can be maintained across microstructure when in reality diffusion and equalization would rapidly eliminate any gradient
failure_modes.evidence: Surface tension gradients equalize on timescales of milliseconds to seconds, making sustained directional transport practically impossible

failure_modes.description: Contradicts established fluid dynamics principles which show Marangoni effects are typically orders of magnitude weaker than capillary forces in microscale transport
failure_modes.evidence: Numerous studies demonstrate that capillary forces dominate microfluidic transport while Marangoni effects are negligible at small scales

failure_modes.description: Fails to account for boundary conditions where environmental humidity, temperature fluctuations, and contamination would overwhelm engineered gradients
failure_modes.evidence: Real-world surfaces experience constant environmental perturbations that would disrupt any carefully engineered surface tension gradients

failure_modes.description: Novelty claim is false as Marangoni-driven transport has been extensively studied and shown to be impractical for sustained directional transport
failure_modes.evidence: Decades of research on Marangoni effects in microfluidics show they're typically used for mixing rather than directional transport

failure_modes.description: The proposed falsifier is inadequate as it only tests one reversal condition while ignoring other confounding variables
failure_modes.evidence: The falsifier doesn't account for alternative mechanisms like electrostatic effects, vibration, or capillary action that could mask true Marangoni behavior

failure_modes.description: The hypothesis is fundamentally incompatible with practical applications due to energy requirements needed to maintain gradients
failure_modes.evidence: Sustaining meaningful temperature/composition gradients would require continuous energy input beyond what's practical for most applications
